title: Accepted Bottom Water-Thermal Substep Carrier Implementation

invariants.assessment: The implementation reuses the existing F-KT/canonical runtime and serialized reference backend. It introduces no second SWAP kernel.
No file, path, parser, format or unit handling is introduced into the kernel or carrier path.
Physical continuation state remains separate from worker-local carrier scratch and candidate-scoped result/provenance metadata.
The carrier is absent from kernel committed state and is not persisted per logical column. Immutable thermal parameters remain in parameter objects.
Carrier samples and route provenance live in the worker/backend model and transaction attempt context, with copy/restore semantics for trial rollback.
Carrier storage is bounded by 2*max_committed_substeps and is allocated only when requested on an admitted thermal route.
Full, half and retry attempts use transaction attempt-context capture/restore. Rejected route samples are removed and a candidate is materialized only after the full outer interval completes.
Enabled-versus-disabled qualification proves identical physical solve counts and candidate state. No extra Richards or thermal solve reconstructs discarded history.
Every carrier sample stores generic t0,t1 values. No day, month, year or midnight assumption is introduced.
The carrier covers the requested generic outer interval and is independent of the duration or calendar placement of a coupling window.
The implementation preserves transaction rollback and accepted interface-transfer provenance needed by coupling without embedding coupler composition into SWAP.
No SWAP-MODFLOW head or flux equality rule is modified. The carrier consumes the existing accepted signed SWAP bottom-water exchange only.

The carrier does not create a second water ledger. Qualification checks that summed carrier exchange equals accepted bottom exchange and that hydrologic mass results are bit-identical with the feature disabled.
Interface-sensitivity production, semantics and publication are untouched.
Qualification checks exact physical solve-count parity between carrier-enabled and carrier-disabled execution.
Carrier memory belongs to a worker/backend execution object, not every logical column, and activation is explicit and optional.
The implementation has no MODFLOW-cell, tile-fraction or area-weighting knowledge.
Bottom exchange is not reinterpreted as deep groundwater recharge. Any deep-vadose transfer component remains outside SWAP.
No component-transition storage or transfer rule is changed; thermal provenance accompanies but does not alter accepted water transfer.
The carrier contract exposes accepted-route transfer samples rather than Richards or HeadCalc arrays. The current production binding is the serialized reference backend only.
The implementation reuses current hydraulic solve results and restricted soil-temperature state instead of duplicating process physics or importing legacy global state.
Bottom thermal data are obtained through typed state/soil-temperature interfaces. No other module is coupled to HeadCalc internal arrays for this feature.
Thermal-carrier activation is an explicit feature/result request. Full/half/retry selection remains numerical policy and does not silently modify physics.
Carrier cost is bounded by configured committed-substep capacity. Missing or invalid provenance invalidates carrier publication instead of causing unbounded extra solving.
Qualification is performed on the full reference execution path, including O0/O2 identity and preservation gates.
Existing runtime solver/retry/mass diagnostics are unchanged. Carrier readiness and thermal completeness are explicit result/provenance properties rather than hidden state.
Carrier allocation and result production occur only when bottom-thermal provenance is requested and restricted soil temperature is active.
The carrier does not know system composition, tile fractions, MODFLOW mapping or transfer-zone routing.
No file format, .swp input, midnight boundary, fixed-duration window or direct-MODFLOW assumption is added.
This implementation-level audit assesses EB-I13 explicitly against all thirty SWAP architecture invariants.

required_attacks: selected two-half route retains no rejected full-route sample
rejected attempt and retry restore the exact carrier checkpoint prefix
accepted multi-transaction outer interval retains one exact ordered sample sequence
failed outer interval after accepted internal progress cannot materialize a full requested-interval candidate
zero transfer needs no donor temperature
local outward transfer retains same-advance start/end bottom temperatures
external inward transfer without external donor temperature remains explicitly incomplete
carrier enablement does not alter physical solve count, hydrologic ledger or candidate physical state
carrier remains absent from F-KT persistent kernel state
hard_nonclaims: external groundwater or deep-vadose donor temperature model
closed soil or land-column energy balance
